newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to buy British Sea Skua missiles - minister.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to buy British Sea Skua missiles - minister.

text.p: Kuwait will go ahead with the purchase of British Aerospace Sea Skua missiles, dropping a French offer, the defence minister said in remarks published on Saturday.

Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah "said that the ministry is going ahead with a deal to purchase the British Sea Skua surface-to-surface missiles as recommended by parliament's Public Funds Protection Committee," the Arab Times reported.

He was responding to a question by a Kuwaiti MP on the deal to arm Kuwait's eight, French-made $500 million fast patrol boats ordered in 1995. His response was carried by Kuwait newspapers on Saturday.
The deal, which has an estimated worth of about $90 million, is also sought by Aerospatiale's MM-15 missiles.
Parliament last year asked the committee to investigate the deal after Kuwait dropped the cheaper French offer.
"Studies undertaken by the Defence Ministry concerning the purchase of the British missiles are adequate and conforms to army regulations and standards," the minister added in his reponse.
He said the British offer included a free gift of 20 missiles and a pledge by London to honour a disputed debt of seven million pounds ($11 million).

The French offered eight free missiles and a commission "in case the deal proceeded smoothly...The company asked whether the ministry will be able to use this amount to promote the missiles," added Sheikh Salem.
He said the French also offered a four percent commission if the missile is sold internationally and five percent if it is picked by another Gulf state.

"The company's stand clearly indicates that the MM-15 missile was not yet accepted internationally. He (Sheikh Salem) pointed out that the missile was neither tested nor used by the French Naval Forces," the Arab Times quoted him as saying.
"The minister declared that the ministry's decision to accept the British missile was final and that the ministry has begun taking necessary measures to conclude the deal," it added.
The Sea Skua was successfully used during the 1991 Gulf War against Iraqi naval units.
